transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because the clinic was kind of concerned about how little I’ve been eating. I don’t know, it doesn’t feel like a huge thing to me, but most days I’ll just have coffee before I go to the warehouse, and then maybe later, after GED class, I might have a yogurt or a few bites of something.

It’s just… sitting down for a whole real meal feels like it messes up what I’m trying to keep in line, if that makes sense. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'messes up what I’m trying to keep in line'? Are you worried about gaining weight or trying to maintain a certain shape or size?

I mean… I wouldn’t say I’m trying to be, like, impossible about it or anything. But yeah, I do get nervous about it.

If I eat something heavier, like fried food from the break room, or if there’s a big plate at church and I eat more than I meant to, I start thinking it’s going to show on me right away. Like people will notice or I’ll notice. Then I kind of can’t stop thinking about it, and I want to check the scale to make sure it didn’t… change things. Does that make sense?
When you're worried about what you've eaten affecting your weight, do you ever try to balance it out by doing something else, like exercising a lot, making yourself vomit, or taking laxatives?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like that.

I mean, if I feel like I ate too much, I might get really uncomfortable and kind of try to be more careful after, but I don’t make myself throw up or anything. And I don’t take laxatives. Exercise… I wouldn’t say I do a lot, really. I’m on my feet at work, but that’s just work.

Is that… is that what you mean?
Do you ever restrict what or how much you eat for an entire day after you’ve eaten something you were worried about?

Um… I guess sometimes, yeah. I don’t really think of it as, like, punishing myself or anything. It’s more that if I feel like I had too much, the next day I just try to keep it really light.

So I’ll have coffee before the warehouse, and then maybe later after GED class I’ll do a yogurt or just a few bites of something. A full meal just feels like it throws everything off, and then I get anxious about it. I know that probably sounds bad… I’m just trying to keep it under control, I guess.

Can you tell me more about what it means for you to 'keep it under control' with your eating? Is it mainly about keeping your weight in check, or is there something else about eating that worries you?

I guess… yeah, it’s mostly about my weight, or what I think is going to happen to it.

Like, if I eat fried food at work or I have a bigger plate at church than I meant to, I start worrying it’s going to show on me right away. I know that probably sounds kind of dramatic, but it feels real in the moment. Then I keep thinking about it after, like I messed something up, and I want to check the scale so I can see if it changed.

I’m not trying to be difficult. I just feel like if I don’t keep an eye on it, it’ll get away from me.
When you worry about eating more than you intended, is it mainly about the calories or weight gain, or does it also feel like it changes how your body looks or how you see yourself?

Um… I think it’s both, maybe. I do worry about the calories and the weight part, but it’s also like… once I’ve eaten more than I meant to, I look at myself different.

Like before class or before softball, if I check in the mirror, my stomach and my thighs can look bigger than they should. I know maybe nobody else would even notice, but I notice it, and then it kind of decides how I feel the rest of the day. Like if I look okay, I feel like I’m doing good, and if I don’t, it feels like I already failed.

I don’t know if that makes sense. I’m not trying to make it sound worse than it is.
When you look in the mirror and feel like you look different after eating more than you intended, does that affect how you feel about yourself overall?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like my whole personality depends on it or anything, but it does kind of affect how I feel about myself.

If I look in the mirror before class or softball and my stomach or thighs look bigger than they should, then it’s like… I feel like I already messed up. And if I think I look okay, then I feel like I’m doing good, like I’m more in control. It can kind of set the mood for the whole day, even though I know that probably sounds silly.
Would you say that how you feel about your weight or body shape has a strong impact on how you feel about yourself as a person?

Yeah… I guess I would say it does. I don’t really like admitting that, because it sounds kind of shallow or like I’m making too much of it.

But when I look in the mirror before class or before softball and my stomach or my thighs look bigger than they should, it can make me feel like I’m failing already. And if they look okay, then I feel like I’m doing good, like I’m more in control.

So… yeah, it can affect how I feel about myself for the whole day, even if I know that probably shouldn’t matter that much.
Would you say that your judgment of yourself is heavily influenced by how you perceive your body weight or shape?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to say it like it’s the only thing about me, because I know that sounds bad, but it does matter a lot.

Like if I look in the mirror before class or softball and my stomach or my thighs look bigger than they should, it kind of makes me feel like I’m failing already. And if they look okay, then I feel like I’m doing good, like I have things under control.

So… yeah, I guess my judgment of myself is pretty tied to that, even though I wish it wasn’t.
